analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 2,201 confirmed cases (99% in DRC) and 866 deaths (99% in DRC). Case fatality ratio 39.3%. Treatment facilities under pressure (85.3% occupancy; 126.2% in North Kivu). Contact follow-up below target (66.9%).

title: UNICEF Democratic Republic of the Congo Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1 – Ebola Outbreak (Bundibugyo Virus), 15 May–30 June 2026 - ReliefWeb

analysis.time: The outbreak was declared on 15 May 2026, with epidemiological data reported as of 12 July 2026, and the situation report covers the period 15 May–30 June 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), specifically Ituri Province (epicentre), North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, and Tshopo provinces, affecting 42 health zones across five provinces. The population includes frontline workers, community actors, and affected individuals such as 8,535 people and 240 children.
analysis.event: An outbreak of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus species, officially declared by the DRC Ministry of Public Health on 15 May 2026. It is the seventeenth Ebola outbreak in DRC and the first caused by the Bundibugyo virus since 2012. WHO declared it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 17 May 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of 12 July 2026, DRC reported 1,963 confirmed cases, including 719 confirmed deaths and 333 recoveries, with a case fatality rate of 36.6%. Ituri accounts for 90% of cases (1,772) and 85% of deaths (608). The outbreak has expanded to Haut-Uélé and Tshopo. Risk is compounded by conflict, insecurity, and limited health system access.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: UNICEF co-leads the RCCE and IPC/WASH pillars, supporting community-based surveillance (27,000 household visits), training 5,740 workers, and reaching over 1 million people with prevention messages. Contact tracing is below target (81.5% nationally, 79.4% in Ituri). UNICEF requires US$119.3 million, with only US$23.5 million mobilized (80% gap). Operational reach is constrained by insecurity and attacks on health personnel.

analysis.brief_en: An Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus was officially declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on 15 May 2026, with WHO designating it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May. As of 12 July, 1,963 confirmed cases and 719 deaths have been reported across 42 health zones in five provinces, with Ituri as the epicentre. UNICEF is leading response efforts, supporting community surveillance, training frontline workers, and providing WASH and case management supplies. However, contact tracing remains below target, and the outbreak has expanded to new provinces. UNICEF requires US$119.3 million for a six-month response plan, with only 23.5 million mobilized, highlighting significant funding gaps and operational challenges in conflict-affected areas.
analysis.summary_en: An Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus was officially declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on 15 May 2026, with WHO designating it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May. As of 12 July, 1,963 confirmed cases and 719 deaths have been reported across 42 health zones in five provinces, with Ituri as the epicentre. UNICEF is leading response efforts, supporting community surveillance, training frontline workers, and providing WASH and case management supplies. However, contact tracing remains below target, and the outbreak has expanded to new provinces. UNICEF requires US$119.3 million for a six-month response plan, with only 23.5 million mobilized, highlighting significant funding gaps and operational challenges in conflict-affected areas.

title: WHO Situation Report No.1: Health emergencies in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (June 2026) - ReliefWeb

analysis.time: Originally published 17 Jul 2026; reporting period June 2026; renewed hostilities in early July 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Eastern Mediterranean Region, including Islamic Republic of Iran, several Gulf countries, Lebanon, Sudan, occupied Palestinian territory, Somalia, Yemen, Syrian Arab Republic, Greater Horn of Africa (six countries), and Gulf Cooperation Council states (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia).
analysis.event: WHO Situation Report No.1 on health emergencies in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (June 2026), released on 20 Jul 2026. The report documents ongoing and renewed health emergencies, including conflict-related impacts, disease outbreaks, and humanitarian crises across multiple countries.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Sudan remains the largest humanitarian emergency with 30.4 million people requiring assistance and 13.5 million displaced, facing multiple concurrent disease outbreaks and severe funding shortfalls. In Lebanon, insecurity and damage to critical infrastructure in South Lebanon and Nabatiyeh constrain humanitarian response. Across other graded emergencies, conditions in occupied Palestinian territory and Somalia continued to deteriorate, while Yemen and Syrian Arab Republic faced strain from conflict, funding constraints, disease outbreaks, and climate-related hazards.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO is appealing for US$6.42 million to sustain critical health and nutrition interventions in Sudan, Somalia, and Djibouti. WHO accelerated regional preparedness for Bundibugyo virus disease through strengthened surveillance, rapid response capacity, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, water, sanitation and hygiene, laboratory preparedness, community engagement, and contingency planning. In Somalia, WHO supported national preparedness planning, readiness assessments, and pre-positioning of viral haemorrhagic fever and laboratory supplies.

analysis.brief_en: On July 20, 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) released Situation Report No.1 covering health emergencies in the Eastern Mediterranean Region during June 2026. The report highlights renewed hostilities in Iran and Gulf countries, including attacks on commercial shipping and disruptions to navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, which increased risks to civilians, medical supply chains, and essential health services. Sudan remains the region's largest humanitarian emergency, with 30.4 million people requiring assistance and 13.5 million displaced, facing multiple concurrent disease outbreaks and severe funding shortfalls. In Lebanon, insecurity and damage to critical infrastructure in South Lebanon and Nabatiyeh continued to constrain humanitarian response. Across other graded emergencies, conditions in occupied Palestinian territory and Somalia deteriorated, while Yemen and the Syrian Arab Republic faced strain from conflict, funding constraints, disease outbreaks, and climate-related hazards. The Greater Horn of Africa experienced a deteriorating food insecurity and health crisis, affecting 37.8 million people. WHO is appealing for US$6.42 million to sustain critical health and nutrition interventions in Sudan, Somalia, and Djibouti. The report details WHO's response, including accelerated regional preparedness for Bundibugyo virus disease, support for cholera preparedness in Sudan, training of health workers in Somalia, and strengthening of emergency health operations across the Region through country-specific support and regional preparedness measures.

title: The African Development Bank Group to provide $13 million to bolster Ebola response – outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan and Uganda

analysis.time: Publication date: 20 July 2026. The approved funding is to enhance national emergency responses to the Ebola virus disease outbreak, which was announced by DRC on 15 May 2026 and has since spread to North Kivu and South Kivu.
analysis.location_and_population: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), specifically Ituri province (including Bunia, Rwampara, and Mongwalu), North Kivu, and South Kivu; South Sudan; and Uganda. The affected population includes communities in the most affected and vulnerable areas.
analysis.event: The African Development Bank Group has approved grants totaling USD 13 million to enhance national emergency responses to the Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak and strengthen efforts to arrest its spread in DRC, South Sudan, and Uganda. The outbreak is confirmed and caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak is centred in DRC, which is the epicentre and will receive USD 11 million of the funding. Uganda and South Sudan will each receive USD 1 million. The outbreak has spread to North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. The Bundibugyo strain is particularly virulent, and there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for it.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The funding is being deployed under the Bank Group’s Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak Response Plan to halt the spread of the virus and reduce related mortality and morbidity. Implementation will be carried out by the World Health Organization (WHO) for the USD 10 million grant and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) for the USD 3 million grant. Activities include strengthening early case diagnosis, epidemiological surveillance, community engagement, public awareness, and regional coordination.

analysis.brief_en: On July 20, 2026, the African Development Bank Group approved a USD 13 million grant package to bolster emergency responses to the Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, and Uganda. The funding, comprising a USD 10 million grant channeled through the World Health Organization and a USD 3 million grant implemented by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, will support early case diagnosis, surveillance, community engagement, and regional coordination. The outbreak, confirmed on May 15, 2026, is centred in DRC's Ituri province and has spread to North Kivu and South Kivu. Caused by the virulent Bundibugyo strain, it currently lacks an approved vaccine or specific treatment.
analysis.summary_en: On July 20, 2026, the African Development Bank Group approved a USD 13 million grant package to bolster emergency responses to the Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, and Uganda. The funding, comprising a USD 10 million grant channeled through the World Health Organization and a USD 3 million grant implemented by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, will support early case diagnosis, surveillance, community engagement, and regional coordination. The outbreak, confirmed on May 15, 2026, is centred in DRC's Ituri province and has spread to North Kivu and South Kivu. Caused by the virulent Bundibugyo strain, it currently lacks an approved vaccine or specific treatment.

title: Osaka Metropolitan University, K.K. DNAFORM, and INRB launch development of a portable rapid diagnostic system for Ebola virus disease - EurekAlert!

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-17. Event date: Development efforts launched immediately after the WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) regarding the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the DRC and Uganda on May 16, 2026 (Geneva time; May 17, Japan time).
analysis.location_and_population: Japan (Osaka Metropolitan University, K.K. DNAFORM), Democratic Republic of the Congo (National Institute for Biomedical Research, INRB), and Uganda. The affected population includes healthcare workers and communities in outbreak areas. The development involves a collaborative network of industry, academia, government, and international partners.
analysis.event: DNAFORM, and INRB are jointly developing a portable rapid diagnostic system, the GenPad Smart BDBV, for detecting Ebola virus disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). The project is under development and evaluation, not intended for clinical use or commercial sale.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The development aims to address the urgent need for rapid, point-of-care testing in outbreak areas with limited medical resources. The prototype met the limit of detection (LOD) target of ≤200 copies per cartridge and showed no cross-reactivity against a panel of 86 microbial species. The system is designed to be portable (460 g), battery-powered, and deliver results in approximately 30 minutes. The project is aligned with the '100-Day Mission' to develop diagnostics within 100 days of identifying a new infectious disease threat.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Initial laboratory evaluation confirmed the prototype met performance criteria. Future plans include performance validation using mock samples and clinical performance validation using clinical samples in the DRC, in collaboration with INRB. The project is supported by the Global Health Innovative Technology Fund (GHIT Fund) and is being conducted in close coordination with the WHO. The product is not intended for clinical use or commercial sale.

analysis.brief_en: Osaka Metropolitan University, K.K. DNAFORM, and the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are jointly developing a portable rapid diagnostic system called the GenPad Smart BDBV for detecting Ebola virus disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus. The system, based on K.K. DNAFORM's SmartAmp isothermal PCR technology, is designed to be battery-powered, portable, and deliver results in approximately 30 minutes. The project was launched immediately after the World Health Organization declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern regarding the BDBV outbreak in the DRC and Uganda in May 2026. The prototype has met initial laboratory performance criteria, including a limit of detection of ≤200 copies per cartridge and no cross-reactivity against a panel of 86 microbial species. The development is aligned with the '100-Day Mission' to provide diagnostics within 100 days of identifying a new infectious disease threat. The project is supported by the Global Health Innovative Technology Fund (GHIT Fund) and is being conducted in close coordination with the WHO. The system is currently under development and evaluation and is not intended for clinical use or commercial sale.

The project is supported by the Global Health Innovative Technology Fund (GHIT Fund) and is being conducted in close coordination with the WHO. The system is currently under development and evaluation and is not intended for clinical use or commercial sale.

title: Makerere scientists identify genetic changes in Ebola Bundibugyo virus - Uganda Observer

analysis.location_and_population: Uganda (Makerere University), Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Affected populations include confirmed cases and deaths in the DRC, and researchers at Makerere University and the Ministry of Health.

analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The DRC has reported 2,344 confirmed Ebola Bundibugyo cases and 930 deaths, the largest recorded outbreak of the strain. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Efforts are underway to develop new diagnostic kits tailored to the circulating strain and to strengthen disease surveillance. Further research is needed to fully establish the effectiveness of available treatments against the evolving virus.

title: New battery-powered device detects Bundibugyo Ebola virus in thirty minutes - News-Medical

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-17. Event date: May 16, 2026 (WHO declared PHEIC), May 17, 2026 (Japan time), and development timeline spanning from the PHEIC declaration to prototype completion in 40 days.
analysis.location_and_population: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda (affected areas), with research collaboration between Osaka Metropolitan University (Japan), K.K. DNAFORM (Japan), and the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB, DRC). The device targets populations in outbreak zones with limited medical resources.
analysis.event: Development of a portable rapid diagnostic system (GenPad smart BDBV) for detecting Bundibugyo Ebola virus (BDBV). The project is funded by the Global Health Innovative Technology Fund (GHIT Fund) and is under development and evaluation, not intended for clinical use or commercial sale.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The device is a prototype with a limit of detection (LOD) of ≤200 copies per cartridge and no cross-reactivity against 86 microbial species. It can perform eight tests on a single charge and provide results in approximately 30 minutes. The development aligns with the WHO's 100-Day Mission to rapidly deploy diagnostics for emerging infectious disease threats.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The prototype has met initial laboratory performance criteria. Future plans include performance validation using mock samples and clinical samples in the DRC, preparation of data for WHO Emergency Use Listing, and parallel development of a multiplex version. The device is currently under development and evaluation, and its clinical utility and regulatory approval are not yet confirmed.

analysis.brief_en: Researchers from Osaka Metropolitan University, K.K. DNAFORM, and the National Institute for Biomedical Research in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have developed a portable, battery-powered rapid diagnostic system called the GenPad smart BDBV. The device, funded by the Global Health Innovative Technology Fund, uses isothermal PCR technology to detect the Bundibugyo Ebola virus in approximately 30 minutes. It is designed for use in resource-limited outbreak areas and has demonstrated a limit of detection of ≤200 copies per cartridge with no cross-reactivity against 86 microbial species. The prototype is currently under development and evaluation, with future plans including clinical validation in the DRC and preparation for WHO Emergency Use Listing. The project aligns with the WHO's 100-Day Mission to rapidly deploy diagnostics for emerging infectious disease threats.

title: As the Ebola outbreak rages, new treatments are headed into trials. Will they work?

analysis.time: The outbreak is reported as ongoing as of mid-July 2026, with the article published on July 20, 2026. The WHO trial enrollment is described as launching now.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is occurring in Congo (Democratic Republic of the Congo) and has affected at least 1,926 people, with more than 700 deaths. The affected population includes patients of any age who are diagnosed with the Bundibugyo virus strain.
analysis.event: The World Health Organization (WHO) is launching its first-ever treatment trial for the Bundibugyo virus strain, which is tearing across Congo. The trial is evaluating the efficacy of two investigational treatments, MBP-134 and remdesivir, both individually and in combination.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of mid-July, the outbreak has killed more than 700 people and infected at least 1,926. The outbreak is described as the fastest-growing in history, with at least 80% of cases originating from unknown transmission chains. The lack of approved treatments for this strain is a critical risk.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO has established a platform trial to test MBP-134 and remdesivir. The trial is open to patients of any age. The effectiveness of both treatments against the Bundibugyo virus is uncertain; preclinical data show promise, but human efficacy has not been established. The source is a full original report from PharmaVoice.

analysis.brief_en: As the Bundibugyo Ebola strain tears across Congo, killing over 700 and infecting at least 1,926 people, the World Health Organization has launched its first-ever treatment trial for this strain. The trial will evaluate MBP-134, a monoclonal antibody cocktail, and remdesivir, an antiviral approved for COVID-19, both individually and in combination. No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for this strain, and the outbreak is described as the fastest-growing in history, with 80% of cases linked to unknown transmission chains. The trial is a platform study open to patients of any age, but the safety and efficacy of both drugs against the Bundibugyo virus remain unproven. The article is a full original report from PharmaVoice.
